answer: Opal Ledger Continuity: each agent must solve a public, memory-hard puzzle chaining its prior signed actions; the chain tip embeds a rotating opal code. Cloning forces replaying every prior puzzle, so cost scales linearly with tenure. New identities restart that chain and pay the full puzzle cost, while honest agents amortize it across history. Onyx scores weight continuity over headcount, and any plume of cloned tips collapses to the shortest chain. Attack cost: one full puzzle pass per clone, per epoch.
